clue.text: Advising company, French one trading

parts.note: un is the French for one
trading goods means selling them

explanation.surface: A French firm's representative gives advice while doing business.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving guidance to someone, especially professionally on personal problems, is a form of advising them.

clue.text: Score hit playing with right singer

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician scoring a hit record with a song that leans to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' shuffles SCOREHIT into CHORISTE, and R is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a church or cathedral choir is a singer.

clue.text: Get one's kit off university doctor wearing cape

indicators.note: the cape is wearing the doctor, so it wraps around those letters

parts.note: a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness

explanation.surface: An academic medic in a cloak strips off.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Get one's kit off' is British slang for removing one's clothes, i.e. stripping.

clue.text: Under cover, sheepdog scratching head in its shade

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, so a letter is removed from the dog

parts.note: a sheltie is a Shetland sheepdog

indicators.note: the head in a word is its first letter

parts.note: red is a shade or colour

explanation.surface: A sheepdog scratching its head while lying in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching' looks like the dog itching, but it removes the I that 'head in its' supplies; a sheltie is a Shetland sheepdog.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere protected from weather or danger is under cover, i.e. shielded.

clue.text: Fun activity that's unpleasant after lady gets half-cut

indicators.note: after places the exclamation behind the shortened lady in the answer
half-cut normally means drunk, but here the word is literally cut in half, keeping its front half

parts.note: ugh is the exclamation of someone finding something unpleasant

explanation.surface: A lady getting tipsy at a party, which turns unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it literally halves the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done just for amusement is 'a laugh' in casual British speech.

clue.text: Consequences of rogue deeds

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal or rogue
acts are deeds or actions

explanation.surface: The results of a villain's misdeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Effects or results produced by an event are its consequences.

clue.text: Divine having time away from visitors

indicators.note: having something done to the visitors here means acting on them, with the time removed
away from says the time letter is taken out of the visitors

parts.note: guests are visitors to a home

explanation.surface: A holy figure taking a break from receiving callers.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to discover by intuition, i.e. to conjecture correctly.

clue.text: Spy James going round large fair

indicators.note: Bond goes round the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: James Bond is Ian Fleming's fictional spy

explanation.surface: James Bond circling a big funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair hair is light-coloured, as is blond hair.

clue.text: Issues from holidays on Scottish river

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: short holidays are breaks
the Forth is a river in Scotland flowing into the Firth of Forth

explanation.surface: Problems arising from vacations by a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that issues comes out suddenly, i.e. erupts or emerges.

clue.text: Tackle some horrible quip men told

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking on a nasty joke some men told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' looks like a verb but is the noun: gear, as in fishing tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is gear or apparatus for a task, such as fishing tackle.

clue.text: Urban residents won't sleep agitated about work

indicators.note: the stirred letters are placed about the work, surrounding it
agitated letters are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: City dwellers kept awake by worry about their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' shuffles WONTSLEEP, and those letters go 'about' OP.
explanation.definitionFit: People living in a town or city are its inhabitants, the urban population.

clue.text: Noted space in hospital department

parts.note: an em is a printer's space
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Room recorded in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone noted is famous and distinguished in their field.

clue.text: Cabin's not opening with a turning tool

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a shack is a cabin; with the 's it becomes shacks

indicators.note: turning means these letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A hut whose door won't open, so a revolving tool is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: SHACK'S loses its first letter to give HACKS; W plus A is reversed by 'turning' to give AW.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw for cutting metal, with a fine blade in a frame, is a type of tool.

clue.text: Coming west, regularly seen sweet dinky birds

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming west means read from right to left
regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: Small cute birds flying in from the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes S, E, T, I, K from SwEeT dInKy, and 'Coming west' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: The kite is a bird of prey, so these are birds.

clue.text: Changes school subject with dreams of the future

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
visions are imagined hopes for what is to come

explanation.surface: A school reforms its curriculum with grand plans for the years ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Amendments made to a text or plan are alterations to it.

clue.text: Aliens from one star base turned up in transport

indicators.note: the reversed letters sit in the vehicles

parts.note: vans are a form of transport

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the sun is a star
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Extraterrestrials from a starbase arriving in a spaceship.
explanation.walkthrough: I, SUN and E are reversed by 'turned up' to give ENUSI, which goes 'in' VANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of the planet Venus would be extraterrestrial beings.

clue.text: Supernatural fiend awfully stoic protecting sect

indicators.note: the shuffled letters protect the sect by surrounding it
awfully suggests these letters are badly arranged

parts.note: a cult is a sect

explanation.surface: A demonic being, terribly calm, shielding a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiend' here means enthusiast or fan, not demon; the shuffled letters from 'awfully' are split around the sect.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is a fanatic, so a fan of the supernatural studies magic and the occult.

clue.text: Vetoed backing of Republican president, Democrat brought in

indicators.note: backing means the word is reversed
the Democrat is brought into the president's name

parts.note: Joe Biden was the US president when this appeared

explanation.surface: A measure blocked by a Republican-backed president with a Democrat on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but reverses the word 'of'; Joe Biden was US president when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vetoed is prohibited, not allowed.

clue.text: Welshman lies after losing leader's keys

parts.note: Ivor is a typically Welsh man's name

indicators.note: the word loses its leading letter and comes after the name

explanation.surface: A Welshman fibbing after his leader is ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivories is informal for piano keys, once made of elephant tusk.

clue.text: Announced means of paying store

indicators.note: announced signals a word spoken aloud with a like sound

parts.note: cash is a means of payment

explanation.surface: A shop announcing which payment methods it accepts.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden store of supplies or valuables, a hoard.

clue.text: Takeaway with baked food beneath counter

indicators.note: in a down clue beneath puts this piece below the other

parts.note: a chip is a gambling counter
a pie is baked food

explanation.surface: Takeaway food with a pie under the shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a chippie is a fish-and-chip shop, a takeaway food outlet.

clue.text: Body oddly peculiar after sport massage

indicators.note: the letters that follow come after the sport

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters

parts.note: peculiar in the sense of particular to oneself, one's own

explanation.surface: An odd-looking body getting a massage after playing sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk rub of the body after exercise is a type of massage.

clue.text: Instrument is article used in tricky job

indicators.note: the article is used inside the shuffled letters
tricky suggests the letters are twisted round

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A musical tool needed for a difficult task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' turns JOB into BJO, and AN goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed musical instrument with a round body, plucked.

clue.text: Beat up Capone, perhaps, in early days

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to tan someone is to thrash or beat them
Al Capone was the gangster; perhaps marks him as one example of an Al

explanation.surface: Beating up the gangster Capone in his youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to birth, the very beginning of life.

clue.text: Strike to fasten joint in arrangement of boards

indicators.note: the strike fastens around the joint, enclosing it

parts.note: to slap is to strike
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Hammering to secure a joint while putting up planks.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlapping or rebated timber cladding, used on walls and boat hulls, is a method of fitting boards.

clue.text: Name of female doctor in theatre

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A woman surgeon working in the operating room.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, the feminine of Henry.

clue.text: Pronounced noses treasured

indicators.note: pronounced signals a word spoken with the same sound

parts.note: to nose is to pry, so noses means pries

explanation.surface: Prominent noses that are highly valued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like an adjective, 'marked', but signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prize, as in a prize bull, is valued highly and cherished.

clue.text: Bad smell around fish, odour on the way out

indicators.note: around means turned about, reversed

parts.note: BO is body odour, a bad smell
a sole is a flatfish
a scent is an odour

explanation.surface: A foul stink around fish, the smell going outside.
explanation.walkthrough: BO (body odour) is the standard British shorthand for a bad smell; 'around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming out of date and falling out of use, i.e. dying out.
